synthesis.evidence_balance: mixed — rising absolute EBITDA, sub-2x stated leverage and double-digit growth offset a sharp idiosyncratic drawdown, a growth miss, dilution and thin FCF.

bull_points.claim: EV/EBITDA at 18.4x sits at the 0th percentile of its own 20-quarter history (near-floor), and the P/E at 112x is explicitly flagged as distorted by an anomalous trailing EPS of 0.21 vs a recent median of -0.54, so the headline P/E is not a clean multiple.

Absolute EBITDA stepped up sharply in the FY2025 readings (29 → 63 → 56) on rising revenue (354 → 389 → 441), so the falling/low EBITDA margin % masks an absolute EBITDA that is RISING — the consensus margin-erosion read is the optical MISREAD, not the real signal.

Name fundamentals beat the peer median on growth — rev growth 18% vs 14%, EBITDA growth 42% vs 21% — with an in-line 13% EBITDA margin, so any TEV/EBITDA discount to the peer median (name 18.4 vs median 24.5; NTM 12.8 vs 17.59) is posed as possibly RESIDUAL rather than EARNED; the human must judge justified-vs-residual, with the caveat that name is EDGAR-GAAP vs peers on CIQ basis (a delta may be definitional).
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Comparable Analysis→Operating Statistics (name vs peer median: growth/margin/leverage/beta)

bull_points.claim: Net leverage fell to 1.8x at Q1 2026 from 4.0x a year prior per management, materially better than the 2.8x screen estimate and the 3.7x peer-comp figure, easing the leverage concern.

bull_points.claim: Consensus target price mean is $42 / median $43, well above where the ~57% 180-day drawdown has left the name, indicating analysts have not re-rated to terminal.

bear_points.claim: The name has fallen 57% over 180 days vs IWM +18%, a ~70-point idiosyncratic relative underperformance, signalling the market is pricing a name-specific impairment rather than a sector move.
Share count is diluting fast — +15.9% over ~1.7 years (41.9M → 48.5M) — eroding per-share value and consistent with equity-funded growth/acquisition needs.

FY2025 GAAP free cash flow is barely positive at $0.8M, and the multi-year FCF series shows two consecutive negative years (FY2023 -16, FY2024 -16) before a thin recovery, so the FCF-positive 'self-funding' claim rests on a razor-thin margin.

On the peer-comp leverage delta the name screens worse than the peer median (Debt/EBITDA 3.7 vs 2.1) — a genuine EARNED-discount input on a trailing basis — though it is OUTWEIGHED by management's stated 1.8x Q1 net leverage and the rising absolute EBITDA that the margin-% optics obscure.

decisive_question.question: Is the Q1 stent-graft/AMDS shortfall a timing problem (VAC-process and PMA-approval delays that reverse as accounts convert) or the start of a structural adoption stall — and does the Endospan acquisition de-risk or further lever the growth story?

evidence_for.claim: Management frames the AMDS miss as starter-set timing, citing encouraging reorder patterns in existing accounts and imminent PMA approval that removes the IRB barrier and the $100K stocking-cost friction — i.e., a timing problem.
evidence_for.source_ref: CIQ transcript(s): Artivion, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 07, 2026.rtf; Artivion, Inc., Q4 2025 Earnings Call, Feb 12, 2026.rtf

evidence_for.claim: Absolute EBITDA and revenue stepped up sharply in the latest FY2025 readings, consistent with the underlying business still compounding through the quarter's noise.

evidence_against.claim: Q1 stent-graft growth missed the company's own expectation across multiple geographies, and the same 8-K that disclosed it triggered the gap-down alongside the Endospan option exercise — raising the question of whether growth requires ongoing acquisition and dilution.

evidence_against.claim: Share count is up 15.9% in ~1.7 years and FY2025 FCF is only $0.8M after two negative years, so the growth story leans on dilution and thin internal cash generation.
